The filament comes up on a landing, a smoke door, and a handrail that ends where handrails end.

Back to the ringing-room landing. The completed rows held.
Bells standing. The service lock releases. Descend to the nave.
The touch comes round. Two rows of rounds remain. Stand clear.
Let go. The seven carry the course until I take the tenor again.
The bells are directly above the inner screen. The corridor is carrying more than sound.
The tower is silent above the nave. The recorder meter is moving anyway. Put the fifth take on tape.
That’s how his box starts.
Those two. The recording is answering the ring.
No bells. Whatever is in there, I go in with the room the way I found it.
The door is shut behind you, oak in the belfry wall. The room is the one it showed; the floor is a floor now, ten metres above the nave.
The chapel’s eight hang here, mouth-down, four over four. Through the trap between them the crossing floor is a pale square a long way down.
Quiet past them. Everything under this floor will hear a bell.
I cannot leave the visit like this. Try again, or get back out.
music-box
Shut, and everything I need is on my back. Nothing in there but a blanket and a road atlas I have not opened since I got the phone.
The shift is ticked on the work order. In ink.
Both leaves go over, and the light inside goes with them. The yard is only what the gate lamp reaches now.
Case, Survey Indicator, and the shift sheet. Finish packing before I sign for the building.
He has told me everything he is going to tell me. The keys are in my pocket and the job is in the basement.
No. Something is holding the key.
It was here. I came through it. It was here.
B3. Marked. Inner door, then down the basement stair. Follow the bearing.
Studio B3. This is the room. The bearing brought me to the door; now I listen.
No. I know this trick: leave the first check till later and later never comes. {BINDINGS.inputPrompt('recorder')}. Six quiet seconds. Then the door.
Levels are good. One thing left: {BINDINGS.inputPrompt('bag')}, plan, mark Studio B3. Then the door.
Before I do something stupid. Eyes shut. Run the worst of it in my head.
Heh.
You open your eyes.
Down at the far end of your light, something starts walking up the beam towards you.
Somewhere ahead of you in the dark, something starts walking towards you.
It walks into you and out the back of you, cold as a cellar step, and keeps going. Whatever it wanted, it wanted the light.
You blink. The room is still here. Your feet are exactly where you left them.
Right. Whatever the hell that was, the light stays off.
Mic first. Say 'check, one, two' and watch the meter. The recorder is stopped. This test is not saved.
There it is. That's me on the meter — and that is exactly what a take hears if I so much as move wrong. Right. Levels.
Nothing here to get behind.
There is a wall here I could put between us, if it comes to that. The torch will help me see, but that hum will carry.
No torch. It has the torch.
My flashlight is still on the workbench.
Flat. And this stair only answered the second click. No second click now—so I leave it by the long way, in the dark.
Flat. It is flat, and I have nothing to put in it.
The case. They are still holding it.
Leave it rolling. I need to hear what reaches the tape.
There. Off.
No recorder. There is no job until I have it back.
Levels are set. Mark Studio B3 in the plan before I start the job.
The nave is not the way in yet. The tower route is still live.
Not from the edge. All I get here is the tile answering itself. It has to be out in the middle of it.
No. {circuit} is still in the cans. That low note is the building, not the room. Kill it at the panel—or ask me again and I will put the mistake on tape.
All right. Their tape, their ballast. I will mark exactly what I heard.
Again. Same room, this time without the building singing through it.
The case. They are still holding it.
No recorder. There is no job until I have it back.

Ellery. {room}. Room tone. Take {ordinal}. {day}.
Four tolls answer from the chapel tower. Stone and floors put distance around them; the corridor gives it back.

The transport clicks off. Somewhere back along the corridor, something that was not listening a minute ago is listening now.

The first bolt takes the school master key. Beside it is a six-letter word lock; its service copy is kept in the gallery.
The word lock releases. The door opens straight into the night. A fire escape is bolted to the outside wall, with school windows falling away below the grating.
The water is too dark to reflect the ceiling. It keeps a shape anyway, low and patient, as if something under it has leaned forward.
Come here.
No. That is not how rooms work.

lines.text: The surface dimples in a line from the deep end to your shoes. Not a wave. A finger drawing a route.
It was full when I left it.
The recorder meter rises before you arm it. The water answers with one wet click, close enough to be inside the case.
Transport stopped, recorder disarmed. That click still moved the meter.
You take one step back. The water follows by exactly one step and then remembers it has no legs.
A room. A pool. A bad memory of a pool.
The water moves like it is still listening.
Black water and something under it. Not with the light off.
The chapel is no longer an available ending in this run.
The collegiate chapel screen is locked from within. Four rooms remain the only honest work.
The screen holds. Above it, the tower is already moving.
Shut. From the other side.
You lower him onto the flags. His full weight stays where you put it.
You take him under both arms. His heels trail; every doorway now has to admit two bodies.
The guard opens RETURNED and puts the pen under your hand. You write your name across the ruled column.
He turns the ledger one line down and writes ALAN beside the weight you are still carrying.
Not mid-take. It has been on that floor for three weeks; it will keep.
Not mid-take. It will keep.
Not the shop. West through the nave. The front doors.
No handle on this side.
Bell chamber. ACCESS RESTRICTED. The maintenance hasp is linked to the inner screen.
The rubber wedge comes free. The closer takes the weight.
Back on the belt. No carrier. / Back on the belt.
Not while the take is held. Find the source.
{circuit.label}. Up. For a second, nothing—then {circuit.serves} remembers electricity. Dim tubes, old ballast. Useful light with a note underneath it.
{circuit.label}. Down. The light goes first. The hum takes another breath to understand.
The lid pocket is empty. I have the cassettes.
Two blank cassettes in the lid pocket, still in their cellophane. {result.added.join(' and ')} on the sheet.
The tin is empty. I took the spare cell.
A spare torch cell. My reserve is too full to take all of it; I can leave it here and come back.
A spare torch cell, still sealed. A quarter charge into the reserve.
The empty sleeve is still in the cart. I did not imagine taking them.
Two alkaline cells in a sealed maintenance sleeve. Wrong department, right torch. Half a night, if I stop spending it on rooms I already know.
The clock hammer is already clear of the tenor. This is full-circle ringing now; the rope below is the only intervention.
The pawl is carrying the louvres, not the bells. Stopping them is a ringing-room job.

It wants to be told what it is holding before it will run it.
The dial has three stops on it and no detent between them.

Open channel.

Move.

{BINDINGS.inputPrompt('light')}. Torch off, stand still, count to twenty, and put it back on.

Small writing beside the soap dispenser.

A caged service ladder. The small brass lock takes Ren's key.
Something is against the ladder landing.
He turns his back to the shelter, sits, and looks past the road to the lit gate, the lodge and Ellery rising behind them.
They all moved. Every chair in the room, together, while I was looking straight at them. That is not a draught and that is not me.
Steel on a music stand, in one of these rooms, throwing the torch straight back at me. Somebody left a tuning fork out.

They followed the torn tape here. Hold still. They close when they hear me.
Something in the building answers that. Not near, yet.

It stopped. Whatever it had of me, it has lost. Not a sound.
Whatever that was, it stopped when the tape did.
It is not coming any more. It is here, and the tape is still running, and then it is not.

You are not going anywhere else. The inner screen is the only thing left in this building that is still where it was. / The floor has stopped going. The Surfer is alive, collapsed beneath the open stone screen. His weight is on the floor until you take it.
West through the nave. Front doors. One threshold at a time.

You walked all that way and brought me the big ones.
